reason:
Part 1 (the Cavendish Maxwell figures) is confirmed. The cited Gulf News article (dated 16 June 2026) states verbatim: "Sharjah's hotels welcomed 2.1 million guests in 2025, a 22% increase", "hotel revenues hit Dh780 millon [sic]" (up 20%), "occupancy reached 78%", "The average daily rate stood at Dh305", "guests staying for an average of two nights", and "Sharjah currently has 10,700 keys across 102 hotels" (Ali Siddiqui, Cavendish Maxwell). An independent outlet, Zawya/TradeArabia (https://www.zawya.com/en/business/travel-and-tourism/sharjah-hotel-guests-rise-22-to-21mln-l4i0guoz), carries the same numbers, noting that 78% and AED305 are described as "current" operating levels rather than full-year averages.

Part 2 ("no SCTDA release with a 2025 source-market split was found") is false. SCTDA published its "Sharjah Hospitality Statistics Report, Year 2025" (Strategy, Research & Statistics Division, dated Jan 2026; PDF created 22 Jan 2026, uploaded March 2026) at https://www.sharjahtourism.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Statistics-Report-Yr-2025.pdf, linked from https://www.sharjahtourism.ae/industry-resources/insights-and-statistics/. I opened and read all 17 pages. It contains a "Top 20 Source Markets" page (Figure 10 and Table 3) with 2025 market shares and growth: Russia 17% (346,983 guests, +24%), India 11% (231,165, +34%), UAE 9% (~187,000, +40%), Oman 7% (~142,000, +20%), China 5% (97,766, +55%), Saudi Arabia 4% (+5%), Egypt 4% (+16%), Pakistan 4% (+20%), Syria 3% (-23%), Iraq 2% (-16%), Jordan 2% (-5%), then Philippines, Kazakhstan, Sudan, UK, USA, Belarus, Kuwait, Bangladesh, Bahrain at about 1% each; a regional split (Asia 27%, Russia/CIS/Baltics 22%, Arab non-GCC 15%, GCC ex-UAE 14%, UAE 9%, Europe ex-CIS 6%, Africa 4%, Americas 3%); quarterly tables for India, China, Russia and GCC; and top-5 nationalities per hotel class. SCTDA also released the Russia figure publicly on 16 June 2026 via Sharjah24 (https://sharjah24.ae/en/Articles/2026/06/16/kmr8).

Additional discrepancy worth flagging: SCTDA's official full-year 2025 KPIs are 2,055,065 guests (+22%), AED 780M revenue (+20%), 102 hotels, "over 10,700 rooms", but occupancy 70% (hotels 73%, hotel apartments 60%), ADR AED 247, RevPAR AED 172, and ALOS 1.95 nights. Cavendish Maxwell's 78% occupancy and Dh305 ADR therefore are not the official full-year averages; they resemble SCTDA's Q4 2025 readings (81% occupancy, ADR AED 303). The Sharjah Executive Council's July 2026 review of SCTDA's 2025 report (https://sharjah24.ae/en/Articles/2026/07/14/KMR14) repeats the 22%, "over 2 million", 102 hotels and AED 780M figures, so those headline numbers originate with SCTDA, not only the consultancy.
corrected_claim: Cavendish Maxwell (as reported by Gulf News, 16 June 2026, https://gulfnews.com/business/tourism/sharjah-hotels-draw-21-million-guests-as-airport-traffic-fuels-tourism-boom-1.500576026) reports 2.1 million Sharjah hotel guests in 2025 (+22%), Dh780 million revenue (+20%), current occupancy of 78%, ADR Dh305, an average stay of two nights, and 10,700 keys across 102 hotels. SCTDA's own "Sharjah Hospitality Statistics Report, Year 2025" (Jan 2026, https://www.sharjahtourism.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Statistics-Report-Yr-2025.pdf) gives the official full-year figures as 2,055,065 guests (+22%), AED 780M revenue (+20%), 70% occupancy (hotels 73%, hotel apartments 60%), ADR AED 247, RevPAR AED 172, ALOS 1.95 nights, 102 hotels and over 10,700 rooms, and it does include a 2025 source-market split: Russia 17% (346,983 guests, +24%), India 11% (231,165, +34%), UAE 9% (+40%), Oman 7% (+20%), China 5% (97,766, +55%), Saudi Arabia 4%, Egypt 4%, Pakistan 4%, Syria 3%, Iraq 2%, Jordan 2%, with a further nine markets at about 1% each; by region, Asia 27%, Russia/CIS/Baltics 22%, Arab non-GCC 15%, GCC ex-UAE 14%, UAE 9%, Europe ex-CIS 6%, Africa 4%, Americas 3%.
